notes:
Top-line: BridgePoint AssistWorks builds agent-facing orchestration for enterprise support centers (healthcare, fintech verticals). Interested in Redwood as primary inference layer for their RAG platform; must meet regulatory & high-reliability needs.

Background / decision drivers:
- Customer-facing agents (live chat + phone) rely on fast, accurate citations for compliance (must show source link in UI).
- Large KB surface: mix of Confluence, Zendesk articles, product docs, legal templates, and call transcripts — freshness important (daily incremental updates).
- Peak loads during product incidents: 2k concurrent agents, spikes up to 5k; current infra underprovisions retrieval layer.
- Strong preference for VPC/private deployment; want option to run retriever on-prem for PHI-containing docs.

Technical requirements (spoken on 2026-03-02 call):
- RAG with provenance: every answer needs source citations + snippet offsets. Customer will fail compliance if citations missing.
- Retriever latency target: median <= 80ms for top-k fetch, p99 under 450ms under typical load.
- Embedding store: want vector DB in VPC with nightly re-index and incremental ingestion pipeline (webhooks from Zendesk/Confluence).
- Freshness SLA: articles updated in source should be reflected in the index within 4 hours (configurable).
- Multi-source retrieval: ability to rank and show per-source confidence; reranker model for surfacing official docs over community posts.
- Tool-calling: agent UI triggers to open tickets, attach citation, and run canned workflow (requires function/tool-calling + idempotent callback guarantees).
- Quality monitoring: automated evals on a set of 2k labeled tickets, regression alerts when F1 drops >3%.

POC scope (proposed): 4 weeks
- Week 0: security questionnaire, DPA, VPC peering prep.
- Week 1: ingest 500k docs (mixed sources), deploy retriever+reranker in dedicated pool, smoke tests.
- Week 2: integrate tool-calling to sandbox ticketing UI, live agent trial (50 agents).
- Week 3: load test to 5k concurrent agent sessions, observe latency/throughput, adjust batching/caching.
- Week 4: evaluation report + decision checkpoint (metrics: citation precision, median latency, cost per 10k messages).

Quotes / call snippets:
- "If we can't show the source and a snippet on every agent suggestion, Legal won't sign off." — Head of Ops
- "Latency spikes are our biggest risk; we need autoscaling that doesn't blow cost." — CTO

Sales notes / objections:
- Price sensitivity: will compare Redwood Dedicated vs self-hosting quantized models on cost per concurrent session.
- Wants a clear fall-back plan during incidents: e.g., lightweight smaller model or cached KB responses.

Action items (CRM-friendly):
- AB: Send tailored POC SOW + estimated cost breakdown by 2026-03-12.
- SE Diego: Draft architecture diagram showing VPC peering, vector DB placement, retriever/kv cache, and reranker flow.
- Legal: Start DPA + security questionnaire; customer to return by 2026-03-20.

Internal notes for Redwood Optimize integration:
- Recommend embedding quantization + batched retrieval to keep token costs down. Suggest pre-warming dedicated GPU pool during known incident windows.
- Add automatic citation freshness monitor: track source last-modified vs index time and surface stale docs to ops.

PCI/PHI considerations:
- Wants on-prem retriever for PHI-containing transcripts; also requires HSM-backed KMS for key material. Mentioned SOC2 + ISO27001 a must.

Risks:
- Legal slowdown -> cannot access any infra for POC.
- If retrieval latency p99 > 600ms under load, pilot will fail.

Summary: High-value mid-market account. Strong fit for Redwood Dedicated + Private path, plus Optimize recommendations. POC likely to convert if Security + latency SLAs are demonstrated.
